name: Galaxie 500
label: Rough Trade
lede: Three Harvard kids, one producer, three albums in three years, and a phone call about plane tickets that ended it.

eras.title: Three Harvard kids and a borrowed drum kit
eras.text: Dean Wareham, Damon Krukowski and Naomi Yang start playing in Cambridge, Massachusetts, a town that never much wanted them. New York wanted them. So did a producer with a basement studio and a habit of playing the flute badly on purpose.

years.src: WBUR: Damon & Naomi Look Back To Galaxie 500 · Wikipedia: Galaxie 500
years.h: Wareham and Krukowski start a band. Yang has never played bass
years.p: Damon Krukowski played on a drum kit lent by a Harvard classmate, Conan O'Brien. Naomi Yang bought a Gibson EB2 at Cambridge Music Center in Porter Square and learned on it.
years.xp:
[[Dean Wareham|a21a3ff2-064c-452d-8aea-3d4039ab70d6]] and Krukowski had been friends since their days at the Dalton School in New York City; the band came together while they were students at Harvard. The name came from a friend's Ford Galaxie 500.

Yang told WBUR she had no idea how to play bass when she started, and ended up playing high on the neck, lines you could sing along to. The band was never a draw at home: WBUR's write-up says they never sold out a club on a weekend night in Boston.

years.src: Wikipedia: Galaxie 500 · Wikipedia: On Fire · Wikipedia: This Is Our Music
years.h: Tugboat: the first single, cut with Mark Kramer
years.p: Galaxie 500 recorded their debut single with [[Kramer|d898e082-70d1-4a86-ac8e-ecdf89892994]], the Shimmy Disc label boss, in February 1988. He would produce every record they made.
years.xp: Kramer's Noise New York studio was home base for the next three years. He also played on the records himself: the credits list cheap organ on On Fire and cheap flute on This Is Our Music.

years.h: Today · Aurora, recorded in July at Noise New York
years.p: The debut album, produced and engineered by Kramer, came out on Aurora Records. A German CD followed in 1989, then a Rough Trade US pressing in 1991.

years.h: CBGB, one night, later a record
years.p: The band played CBGB in New York on December 13, 1988. A recording of the night was announced for release in 2025 as CBGB 12.13.88.
years.xp: The 2025 release follows Uncollected Noise New York '88-'90, an archival set that came out in 2024. The date comes straight from the release title.

eras.title: Rough Trade takes them in, John Peel plays them
eras.text: London does what Boston wouldn't. A Rough Trade contract, a pair of Peel sessions and a record that lands at number 7 on the UK indie albums chart.

years.h: London signs them: Rough Trade and a UK tour
years.p: The band toured the UK from late 1988 into 1989 and signed to Rough Trade Records, the label that would release their next two albums.

yt: Don't Let Our Youth Go to Waste, Peel Session
years.h: John Peel plays them. Twice, on the record
years.p: Peel had them in for two sessions on BBC Radio 1. Their cover of [[Jonathan Richman|bae34b81-9abd-416e-a720-fedc359df775]]'s Don't Let Our Youth Go to Waste was voted number 41 in the 1989 Festive 50.
years.xp: The Peel sessions were collected on the 2005 album Peel Sessions. The Richman song later lent its title to the 2004 two-disc DVD about the band.

years.h: On Fire lands on Rough Trade and hits number 7 on the UK indie chart
years.p: Kramer produced it again at Noise New York. Pitchfork gave it a 10, and put it at number 16 on its 2002 list of the top 100 albums of the 1980s.
years.xp: UK critics loved it. US press was mixed, with some reviews citing Wareham's vocals as a limit. The Rolling Stone Album Guide later called it the band's best album by far.

eras.title: The record that wasn't fun to make
eras.text: This Is Our Music comes out in September and closes the run. By Dean Wareham's account, the friction had already moved onto the road.

years.src: Wikipedia: This Is Our Music · Wikipedia: Galaxie 500
years.h: This Is Our Music · Rough Trade, the last studio album
years.p: Recorded at Noise New York with Kramer, who played flute. Naomi Yang sings lead on Listen, the Snow Is Falling.
years.xp: Wareham later said making it had been very difficult, and that Columbia Records had been interested in signing them. The album charted on the UK Independent Album Breakers list in 2010 after the reissues, at number 18.

years.src: On Some Bands That Don't Like Each Other I: The Breakup of Galaxie 500 · Dean Wareham : Black Postcards
years.h: A spotlight in Los Angeles, and who should stand where
years.p: Wareham's memoir Black Postcards recalls friction over Krukowski's tour management: hotel rooms, seat assignments, and a Los Angeles show where Krukowski objected to where Wareham stood.
years.xp:
The account comes second-hand here, from a fan-site retelling of Black Postcards. Wareham also writes of being outvoted by the other two, according to a review of the book at QRO.

We did not find a matching account of the LA show from Krukowski or Yang.

eras.title: Don't buy the tickets to Japan
eras.text: A show at a college radio station in Maine, then a Monday morning phone call. Two accounts of the same three days, and they never quite meet.

years.src: GALAXIE 500 have split (30 years on) · Galaxie 500 have split (35 years on) · Wikipedia: Galaxie 500
years.h: Last show: Bowdoin College, Maine, for the campus station WBOR
years.p: About 40 to 50 people saw it, after an opener ran long and left the band waiting in the green room.
years.xp:
The show came at the end of a Cocteau Twins tour. Wareham remembers sitting in that green room getting more and more irritated. He says he made it through the set, loaded his gear into his blue 75 Dodge Dart, and drove all the way home to New York City.

Dan Pearson's letter and the Bowdoin Orient are the sources for the show details.

q: Don't buy the tickets to Japan because I was leaving the band.
years.src: GALAXIE 500 have split (30 years on) · Galaxie 500 have split (35 years on) · On Some Bands That Don't Like Each Other I: The Breakup of Galaxie 500
years.h: Krukowski calls about plane tickets. Wareham quits.
years.p: On Monday morning, Damon Krukowski rang Dean Wareham to book flights for a Japan tour. Wareham told him not to.
years.xp:
Krukowski, 1997, to Ptolemaic Terrascope: Wareham quit more or less out of the blue, on the telephone, with no explanation. Melody Maker reported the split on May 4, 1991, quoting Krukowski saying one day they were planning a Japan tour and the next day Wareham just quit.

Naomi Yang, in Temperature's Rising in 2012: she felt completely stripped of her musical identity, and could not believe Wareham could throw everything away so carelessly without wanting to discuss it. In the same account she says she told him he was lazy and a selfish coward.

Wareham, in Black Postcards: he had been up about an hour, with that sick, nervous feeling, and that this time it was real. He writes that he regrets it ended badly, but that is how things often end. Three days of angry phone calls followed.

eras.title: Two answers, and a box set
eras.text: Wareham starts Luna. Krukowski and Yang answer as Pierre Etoile, then Damon & Naomi, and eventually buy the records back.

years.src: GALAXIE 500 have split (30 years on) · Wikipedia: Galaxie 500
years.p: Krukowski and Yang's first record without Wareham was More Sad Hits, released under the name Pierre Etoile. Asked in 2012 how he felt when Wareham quit, Krukowski's answer was to point at it.
years.xp:
Krukowski, Temperature's Rising, 2012: How did I feel when Dean quit? Are you kidding? Listen to More Sad Hits. Yang told the same magazine it took a long time to recover.

The duo became Damon & Naomi, with the first two records produced by Kramer. They also co-founded the small press Exact Change.

years.p: [[Dean Wareham|a21a3ff2-064c-452d-8aea-3d4039ab70d6]] formed [[Luna|dda04604-b50a-4bd1-8780-77564c659dc0]] after leaving, and the band's debut Lunapark came out in 1992. Before that he put out a solo single, Anesthesia, in February.
years.xp: He had also spent time producing Mercury Rev after the split. Luna would run for years, and Wareham would go on to Dean & Britta and a solo record, Foolproof.

years.h: Krukowski and Yang buy the masters at auction
years.p: Rough Trade went bankrupt in 1991. Krukowski and Yang bought the three albums' masters at auction and reissued them on Rykodisc as a box set, with a disc of rarities.
years.xp: The Rykodisc reissue campaign covered all three albums plus rarities. The Portable Galaxie 500 best-of followed in 1998, and Uncollected, more rarities, in 2004.

years.h: The DVD: Don't Let Our Youth Go to Waste, 1987-1991
years.p: A two-disc DVD of live footage and archive material, named for the Jonathan Richman song the band covered.

years.src: Wikipedia: Dean Wareham · Dean Wareham : Black Postcards
years.h: Black Postcards, Wareham's memoir, on Penguin Press
years.p: The book runs from Wareham's New York high school in the 1970s through Galaxie 500 and [[Luna|dda04604-b50a-4bd1-8780-77564c659dc0]] to his divorce. It is where his version of the split sits in print.
years.xp: A review at QRO describes him feeling outvoted by Krukowski and Yang, and gives Kramer's wild antics a chapter of their own.

years.h: Wareham tours as "Dean Wareham plays Galaxie 500"
years.p: He announced in June 2010 a tour of only Galaxie 500 songs, without Krukowski and Yang. Neither of them joined him.
years.xp: Wikipedia's Wareham page dates the tour to 2011; the Galaxie 500 page says he announced it in June 2010 for that autumn.

years.h: Tugboat turns up in The Perks of Being a Wallflower
years.p: Stephen Chbosky's film uses the song. Neutral Milk Hotel's Naomi, off On Avery Island, was written about Yang, who made a video for it in 2011.
Archival recordings from Kramer's studio, released in 2024. A live set from CBGB, dated 12.13.88, was announced for 2025.
